## Welcome

This is an course on **methods for monitoring biodiversity**, especially for **estimating species' distributions** and **estimating species' population sizes**

\vspace{1em}

| Day | Session | Topic |
|:----|:--------|:------|
| 1 | 0 | Course outline |
| 1 | 1 | Introduction to Biodiversity Monitoring and R |
| 1 | 2 | Plot sampling |
| 2 | 3 | Occupancy Modelling |
| 2 | 4 | Species Distribution Models |
| 3 | 5 | Distance Sampling |
| 3 | 6 | Spatial Capture-Recapture Models |
| 3 | 7 | Conclusion and Next Steps |

## Welcome

- Most sessions have four components:
   1. **theory** lecture (slides, instructor-led)
   2. **practical** lecture (slides, instructor-led)
   3. **coding** practice (participant)
   4. **interactive games** (participant)

\vspace{0.5em}

- More theoretical or advanced material indicated by "*"

\vspace{0.5em}

- This course specifically developed for monitoring biodiversity **in Southern Kyrgyzstan**.

\vspace{0.5em}

- We use relevant species for case studies and examples.

\vspace{0.5em}

- All examples and data are **hypothetical** and **simplified** to fit into the allocated time. Real world surveys are usually more complex.

## Welcome

- The goal of this *workshop* is to **train the trainers** by giving you the **teaching materials** and **the knowledge** needed to pass on to others.

\vspace{0.5em}

- The goal of this *project* is to **develop biodiversity monitoring capacity** in Kyrgyzstan.

\vspace{0.5em}

- Targets two main audiences: university students and conservation practitioners.

\vspace{0.5em}

- We want you to leave feeling that you can pass on this material (possibly after some extra work)

\vspace{0.5em}

- \alert{Your feedback is very welcome!}

Workshop material: 

1. Download from <https://github.com/iandurbach/biodiversity-monitoring-course-mini>
2. Click on green `<Code>` button, select "Download .zip"
3. Unzip into dedicated `biodiversity` workshop folder
4. Find and open (double-click) `biodiversity_monitoring.Rproj`. This opens the project in RStudio.
5. Install required packages by typing the following into the RStudio console: `source("install_workshop_packages.R")`
